caption: The model has two parallel sub-models, one for hypertension (HTN) and one for diabetes (DIA), each following the same structure shown in the steps below.

Households move between being eligible-but-not-enrolled in CBHI, enrolled as CBHI beneficiaries, or fee-waivered. Separately, people at risk of the condition become an untreated NCD population once identified.

Enrolled and fee-waivered households gain health insurance coverage. Facilities earn internal revenue from user fees and reimbursement, at a rate set by the reimbursement approval rate, and untreated cases can become treated NCD.
CBHI premiums and reimbursement requests from insured households generate CBHI revenue, which in turn affects the reimbursement approval rate paid to facilities.
Screening identifies people at risk of the condition, and health care utilization together with care capacity determine how many untreated cases become treated.
Care capacity is further shaped by essential medication availability, funded by public drug funds, and by the number of health care providers, completing the full model structure.
